title: Base change of a filtered colimit of algebras, elementwise
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I$ a small filtered category and $i\mapsto A_i$ a functor from $I$ to the category of commutative $R$-algebras, with transition maps $A(u):A_i\to A_j$ for $u:i\to j$, colimit $A=\varinjlim_IA_i$ in that category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and coprojections $\iota_i:A_i\to A$. Let $N$ be an $R$-module, and put $\gamma_i=\iota_i\otimes\mathrm{id}_N:A_i\otimes_RN\to A\otimes_RN$ and $\gamma_u=A(u)\otimes\mathrm{id}_N:A_i\otimes_RN\to A_j\otimes_RN$. Then (1) every element of $A\otimes_RN$ is $\gamma_i(t)$ for some $i\in I$ and some $t\in A_i\otimes_RN$; (2) if $t\in A_i\otimes_RN$ satisfies $\gamma_i(t)=0$, then $\gamma_u(t)=0$ for some morphism $u:i\to j$ of $I$. (Equivalently, $A\otimes_RN$ with the maps $\gamma_i$ is a colimit of the diagram $i\mapsto A_i\otimes_RN$ of $R$-modules.) When $N$ is a commutative $R$-algebra, the $\gamma_i$ and $\gamma_u$ are ring homomorphisms.

proof.text: *Step 1 ($A$ is the colimit of the $A_i$ as $R$-modules).* By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-underlying-module], applied to $R$, the small filtered category $I$ and the diagram $i\mapsto A_i$ of commutative $R$-algebras with its colimit $(A,(\iota_i))$, the $R$-module $A$ with the $R$-linear maps $\iota_i$ is a colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of the diagram of $R$-modules $i\mapsto A_i$ with transition maps $A(u)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00D6 (lemma-directed-colimit, line 778), via the node cited; the passage from algebras to modules is implicit in More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0AH1

proof.text: *Step 2 (tensoring with $N$; the 'equivalently' form).* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-commutes-with-colimits] to the ring $R$, the small category $I$, the diagram of $R$-modules $i\mapsto A_i$ (transition maps $A(u)$) with the colimit $(A,(\iota_i))$ of step 1, and the $R$-module $N$. It says that $A\otimes_RN$ with the maps $\iota_i\otimes1=\gamma_i$ is a colimit, in the category of $R$-modules, of the diagram $i\mapsto A_i\otimes_RN$ with transition maps $A(u)\otimes1=\gamma_u$. In particular $\gamma_j\circ\gamma_u=\gamma_i$ for $u:i\to j$. This is the parenthetical 'equivalently' clause of the statement.

*Step 3 (elements and zero elements come from a stage: (1) and (2)).* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] to the ring $R$, the small filtered category $I$ and the diagram $i\mapsto A_i\otimes_RN$ of $R$-modules with its colimit $(A\otimes_RN,(\gamma_i))$ from step 2. Its part (1) says that every element of $A\otimes_RN$ is $\gamma_i(t)$ for some $i\in I$ and $t\in A_i\otimes_RN$: this is (1). Its 'in particular' says that for $t\in A_i\otimes_RN$ with $\gamma_i(t)=0$ there is a morphism $u:i\to j$ of $I$ with $\gamma_u(t)=0$ (the transition map along $u$ being $\gamma_u$): this is (2).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00D6 (lemma-directed-colimit, line 778) and Lemma Tag 00D7 (lemma-zero-directed-limit, line 811), in the filtered form of the node cited (filtered to directed: Categories, Lemma Tag 0032, lemma-directed-category-system)

proof.text: *Step 4 (the ring structure when $N$ is an algebra).* Let $N$ be a commutative $R$-algebra. Each $\iota_i:A_i\to A$ and each $A(u):A_i\to A_j$ is a homomorphism of commutative $R$-algebras (they are morphisms of the category of commutative $R$-algebras). By [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-map-ring-hom] applied to $f=\iota_i$, resp. $f=A(u)$, the maps $\gamma_i=\iota_i\otimes\mathrm{id}_N$ and $\gamma_u=A(u)\otimes\mathrm{id}_N$ are homomorphisms of $R$-algebras, in particular ring homomorphisms.
